stem: The weights of packets follow a normal distribution with mean 500 g and standard deviation 20 g. Use P(0 < Z < 1) = 0.3413. What is the probability that a packet weighs between 480 g and 520 g?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Using only one half of the symmetric interval, reporting P(0<Z<1) = 0.3413 instead of doubling it.
Computing P(Z<1) = 0.5 + 0.3413 = 0.8413, answering the cumulative probability below z=1 instead of the two-sided interval.
Computing P(Z>1) = 1 - 0.8413 = 0.1587, finding the upper tail beyond one standard deviation instead of the central interval.

explanation:
1. Standardise: z = (520 - 500)/20 = 1 and z = (480 - 500)/20 = -1.
2. The stem gives P(0 < Z < 1) = 0.3413.
3. KEY STEP: By symmetry of the normal distribution, P(-1 < Z < 1) = 2 × 0.3413 = 0.6826.
4. The interval is symmetric about zero, so both halves contribute equally.

explanation_sections.punchline: 480 and 520 are each 20 g away from the mean 500, so the z-scores are -1 and +1. By symmetry, the total probability is simply 2 times 0.3413 = 0.6826.
explanation_sections.approach: For a two-sided interval around the mean, standardise both limits first. If the two z-scores are mirror images (one positive, one negative with the same magnitude), the probability is 2 times P(0 < Z < z). The stem always gives the one-sided area, so doubling is the only extra step.
explanation_sections.lesson: When an interval is symmetric about the mean, double the one-sided table value. Do not add 0.5 and do not look up a two-sided entry: just multiply by 2.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60 seconds. This is an L1 item. Compute both z-scores in 10 seconds, confirm they are plus and minus 1, then double the given value. Reject option (3) in five seconds: it is the one-sided area, not the two-sided answer.
